newsitem.title: UK: Brent sellers eye paper plays, tussle over price.
newsitem.headline: Brent sellers eye paper plays, tussle over price.

text.p: North Sea crude sellers tussled over the price of Dated Brent on Friday as they tried to force it into line with their paper positions, traders said.
The major that sold an August 6-8 loading cargo at August paper plus 17 cents, one of two done at that price, later sold an August 10-12 loader to a Wall Street trader at August parity.
Traders said the second deal 17 cents cheaper appeared to be an attempt to shift the price of Dated to a level more conducive to the major's short swaps position for next week.
Some added that parity was closer to real market level for wet Brent.
Physical has been forced up this week by a French and U.S. refiner who were seen long short-term swaps.
"They (the major) wanted to bring the Dated down next week but they'll have a hard job because there are a lot of companies out there long," said one trader.

The U.S. refiner appeared to have downscaled attempts to shift two million barrels of Brent trans-atlantic, with just one LR2 seen fixed to the U.S. Gulf. It may still be one Brent short to fill the vessel, traders added.
But apart from the Brent manoeuvring trade in physical and cash crude North Sea markets was quiet.
Spreads and swaps held steady and non-Brent crude held on to high values.

An Ekofisk loading August 17-19 changed hands at a strong 34 cents over Dated Brent, higher than prices charged in the flurry of activity on Thursday that saw as many as half a dozen cargoes of the same grade traded.

With Iraqi exports not expected until mid-August at the earliest refiners have moved to cover requirements. But forward purchasing has been cautious, since Iraqi exports, when resumed, may run at a price-crushing 1.5 million barrels a day.

Nonchalance over the Iraq situation and fund buying in the U.S. helped push up IPE Brent, which settled nine cents higher at $18.54 a barrel at the end of a trading day shortened by exchange power problems.
Sept/Oct hitched up a cent to trade at -4 cts, while Aug/Sept found higher ground overnight in the U.S. aftermarket, moving at +18 cts.
Contracts for differences for next week (July 28-Aug01) were bid about three cents higher at Sept +10 cts, while the following week (Aug 4-8) moved at September -5 cents.

In the Mediterranean, Russian Urals barrels were still valued around Dated Brent minus 65 cents, the level at which an early August cargo traded on Wednesday. The market was balanced between tight avails and weakening buying interest, traders said.

Most of the first decade August Urals programme has been sold, but poor refining margins are detering buyers and have already forced 10 percent run cuts at the ISAB's 230,000 barrel per day Sicilian refinery. -- Sean Maguire, Rosalind Russell, London newsroom +44 171 542 (c) Reuters Limited 1997
